paragraphs.text: SSH-tunnelled multi-protocol model provider for DeepSeek Harness
# dsh-llm-ssh-tunnel
An SSH-tunnelled, multi-protocol model provider for DeepSeek Harness, with a browser settings card.
It exists for the common home-lab shape: **sub2api runs on the NAS, the NAS is not exposed to the pu
blic internet, and DSH may be running somewhere else.** The provider opens an in-process SSH forward
and sends every model request to a loopback port, so sub2api never needs a public listener.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The route is a normal `LlmAdapter`: model selection, tools, images, replay, reasoning effort, token
accounting, and retries behave the same as any other DSH provider. The OpenAI and Anthropic wire con
versions are reused from the public `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` adapter.
Verified with DSH 0.2.1-rc.5 against a live sub2api deployment: discovery, streaming, all three wire
protocols, and image input round-tripped through the tunnel. The automated suite uses an in-process
`ssh2` server, so it needs no NAS credentials and no system `ssh`.
## Project status
`0.2.x` is a beta plugin. The transport, credential handling, discovery, settings card, and all thre
e protocols are covered by the test suite and have been exercised against a live deployment. Interfa
ces may still change before `1.0`.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.5` or a compatible build
- Node.js `^22.19.0` or `>=24.0.0`
- A Web pro

file for the settings card; the model route works without it
- An SSH account that can reach sub2api
's loopback listener
## Why in-process SSH?
The transport is `ssh2`, not the operating-system `ssh` command. That means:

- Windows, Linux, and macOS use the same code path.
- No OpenSSH client installation, no `ssh.exe`,

no `/dev/null` config workaround.
- Key files, passphrases, password auth, and ssh-agent/Pageant are

handled in-process.
- The forward is bound to `127.0.0.1` only.
The trade-off is that `ssh2` does **not** read `~/.ssh/config`. Use explicit `host`, `port`, `user`,
and `identityFile` fields (the settings card asks for them), or fill them in YAML.

`pnpm run build` work as well.
Or pack it and install the tarball:

The package ships a built `lib/`, including the browser bundle. Restart or refresh the Web UI after
ships a built `lib/`, including the browser bundle. Restart or refresh the Web UI after installing.
A link install runs the checkout's `lib/`, so after pulling changes run `pnpm run build` again and r
estart `dsh web` — the Host half is loaded once per process.
## Configure
Add the provider to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (or pass it with `--patch`):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then open **Settings → Plugins → SSH tunnel provider**. The card edits the same connection facts plu
s the sub2api API key, with no YAML edit or restart:

- SSH host, port, user
- private key file path
- known_hosts path
- host-key policy
- sub2api host,

port, API base path
- API key reference and the key itself
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
- `apply()` allocates a loopback port, registers one `LlmAdapter` route, and starts an `SshTunnel`.
- `SshTunnel` owns one `ssh2.Client` and one local TCP server. Each accepted connection opens a `dir

ect-tcpip` channel to `remote.host:remote.port` and pipes the sockets.
- Readiness is a real TCP con
nection through the forward, not just a live SSH client. A dropped connection closes the listener an

d reconnects with exponential backoff (1s → 30s).
- A request that arrives during a reconnect waits

up to `requestTimeoutSeconds`, then fails with `TUNNEL_UNAVAILABLE`.
- Host keys are checked against
`known_hosts`; `accept-new` pins an unknown host after the first successful connection. A changed k

ey is refused.
- The settings card talks to one loopback-only, token-guarded route (`/plugins/dsh-ll
m-ssh-tunnel/config`). The token is fetched by the same-origin page; the route rejects cross-origin

POSTs and requests without the token.
- Connection settings are applied live: an SSH/remote change r
estarts only the forward; a model/knob change rebuilds the catalog/profile. The provider route is ne
forward; a model/knob change rebuilds the catalog/profile. The provider route is never unregistered.
## Security notes
- The settings route is loopback-only. It works when the Web UI is opened as `http://127.0.0.1:...`
or `http://localhost:...`; opening DSH through a LAN address makes the card's own `Host` non-loopbac
k, so the route refuses it (the model route is unaffected).

- The forward binds to `127.0.0.1`, never `0.0.0.0`.
- `apiKeyEnv` is a reference. The key is resolv
ed per request through the DSH credential service (or launch environment) and is never written to th

e settings document or logs.
- The settings route requires a per-process CSRF token and a loopback `

Host`/`Origin`.
- `strictHostKeyChecking: no` accepts an unknown host key; a key already pinned in `
known_hosts` that no longer matches is still refused. Use it only for disposable test environments.
- The ssh2 client inherits the DSH process environment; the API key is not placed on any command lin
The ssh2 client inherits the DSH process environment; the API key is not placed on any command line.
## Limitations

- No `~/.ssh/config` aliases, `ProxyJump`, or interactive keyboard/2FA prompts.
- No PuTTY `.ppk` ke

ys; convert to OpenSSH/PEM.
- Plain HTTP only. An HTTPS sub2api endpoint would present a certificate
for the NAS name, not `127.0.0.1`; terminate TLS on the NAS loopback or use a trusted certificate a

nd a hostname that resolves to loopback.
- This build registers one settings-card route per DSH proc
ess. One SSH-tunnel provider entry is the supported shape; a second entry still serves model calls b

ut cannot share the settings card.
- `GenerateOptions.stop` is rejected by the pi-ai adapter (`UNSUP

PORTED_OPTION`).
- Discovery is advisory metadata. Models that publish no capacities get the configu
red defaults; vision models usually need `input: [text, image]` explicitly.
## Security

See SECURITY.md for the security model and the private reporting
path. Do not open a public issue co

ntaining an API key, private key, host name,
or `known_hosts` contents.
